findings.area: mobile / parent area lock (spec P3, AC_ACCESS_07)
findings.title: Leaving the app or tapping 'Lock parent area' only revokes the server step-up: the open parent screen stays up with its data, and every other parent screen still opens without a PIN until the 300 s window runs out
findings.description: When the app goes to the background in parent mode, app-session.ts:61-68 calls clearAdultCaches() and relockOnServer(). useRelockOnBackground (ui.tsx:295-297) also calls lockParentArea(api). Neither one calls forgetParentUnlock() or navigates anywhere. The parent screens keep their data in component state (useLoad in ui.tsx), which clearAdultCaches does not touch: only resources.tsx and revenuecat.ts register clearers. useParentAccess (ui.tsx:262-287) checks parentUnlockActive() once, at mount. The 'Lock parent area' buttons (home.tsx:241, unlock.tsx:195) also only call lockParentArea, so they have the same gap. The read routes behind these screens need only requireParent, not a recent unlock: GET /v1/family (family.ts:59), /v1/devices, /v1/assignments (homework.ts:1124) and /v1/safety-reports (privacy.ts:729). Their Refresh/Try-again buttons therefore keep working on a screen that is still mounted, however long ago the unlock was. The unlock screen tells the parent otherwise: 'The unlock lasts a few minutes and ends when you lock or leave the app' (unlock.tsx:127). The existing test (app-session.test.ts:127) only checks that a server relock happens.
findings.repro: Code path, no device needed. 1) Shared iPad: the parent taps Grown-ups, enters the PIN and opens Privacy and data (safety reports) or the parent home. 2) The parent presses Home, or taps 'Lock parent area' and sees 'Locked.', then hands the iPad to Riley. 3) Riley reopens PencilLift. The same parent screen is still showing, with the family, devices and safety-report data. Pull-to-refresh and Try again still load fresh data, because those GETs need no step-up. For the rest of the 300 s window (ADULT_UNLOCK_TTL_SECONDS default, config.ts:214) the header links open every other parent screen, because parentUnlockActive(new Date()) is still true. Only mutations fail, with STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
findings.evidence: grep: forgetParentUnlock is called only from mode.ts:54 (enterChildMode), :95 (signOutParent) and :107 (unpairChildDevice). It is never called from app-session.ts or from ui.tsx useRelockOnBackground/LockButton. app-session.ts:61-68: `if (next !== 'background') return; ... clearAdultCaches(); await modeEffects.relockOnServer()`. Clearers are registered only at resources.tsx:197 and revenuecat.ts:142. BUG-129's known-limit note covers only a lapse in the foreground, not backgrounding.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the app one 'lock parent area' action for backgrounding and for both Lock buttons. It should call forgetParentUnlock() and then router.replace('/(parent)/unlock'), or dismissAll first. Have useParentAccess re-check parentUnlockActive whenever AppState returns to 'active'. Keep the Android store purchase sheet working: it pauses the activity and fires 'background'. Either skip the relock while runPlanChange is in flight, or note that the verify step, POST /v1/billing/sync, needs no step-up. Add regression tests: parentUnlockActive is false after a background event in parent mode, and after either Lock button.
findings.userImpact: On a shared family tablet, the parent area stays open to the child after the parent leaves the app or taps Lock. The child can read family, device, homework and safety-report data, even though the screen says the unlock has ended.

findings.title: The child access token's expiry is judged by the device clock against a server-clock timestamp, and a 401 never triggers a refresh. A tablet whose clock is 15+ minutes slow shows 'This device isn't connected yet' for long stretches; one that is 15+ minutes fast rotates the refresh token on every call and hits the 60-per-hour refresh limit
findings.description: persist() stores expiresAtMs = Date.parse(response.accessTokenExpiresAt), which is server time plus 900 s (config.ts:215; child-auth.ts:54). accessToken() then compares it with deps.now(), the device clock, using a 30 s skew (line 97). The server verifies with jose and no clock tolerance (auth/child.ts:45-49). Slow clock: the client keeps sending a token the server already rejects, and a 401 on a data call never drops `access` or refreshes. Child home maps the 401 to 'not_connected': 'This device isn't connected yet. Ask a grown-up for a connect code.' /pair then says 'This device is connected to Riley's space', because isPaired() is still true. That repeats for up to the skew in every 15-minute cycle. Fast clock: every token already looks expired, so each sequential call does a refresh, which rotates the token and writes the keychain. The server allows 60 refreshes per session per hour (rate-limit.ts:119), so a normal practice set exhausts it. After that, refresh throws RATE_LIMITED and every child call fails ('Let's take a little break') for the rest of the hour. Kids setting a tablet clock forward is a common game cheat.
findings.repro: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/mobile-r2/probe-skew.mts runs the real createChildSession and createApiClient against a labeled mock server that issues 15-minute tokens stamped with server time and rejects expired ones. Run it with `cd apps/mobile && npx tsx <probe>`.
findings.evidence:
Output (probe-skew.out):
`device clock correct     : t+0m ok | t+16m ok | t+20m ok | t+40m ok refreshes= 2`
`device clock 20 min slow : t+0m ok | t+16m UNAUTHENTICATED | t+20m UNAUTHENTICATED | t+40m ok refreshes= 1 stillPaired= true`
`device clock 20 min fast : ... refreshes= 4` (one refresh per call)
child-session.ts:67-69 `expiresAtMs: Date.parse(response.accessTokenExpiresAt)`; :97 `access.expiresAtMs - EXPIRY_SKEW_MS > deps.now().getTime()`; (child)/home.tsx:53-56 maps UNAUTHENTICATED to not_connected.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure the lifetime relative to the device. Either add expiresInSeconds to the response or subtract the response Date header, and store expiresAtMs = deviceNowAtReceipt + lifetime. In the token source or client wrapper, when a data call returns UNAUTHENTICATED with a cached access token, clear `access` and retry once through the single-flight refresh. Only forget the pairing if the refresh itself returns UNAUTHENTICATED. Add unit tests with a skewed `now`.
findings.userImpact: On a tablet with a wrong clock, the child is repeatedly told the device isn't connected, or is rate-limited out of homework and practice, even though the pairing is fine.

findings.title: A device clock more than 5 minutes fast makes the parent area impossible to open: each correct PIN leads back to the unlock screen, with no message
findings.description: enterParentMode stores parentUnlockedUntilMs = Date.parse(proof.unlockedUntil). That value is the DB clock plus ADULT_UNLOCK_TTL_SECONDS (300 s; adult.ts:168-172). parentUnlockActive(new Date()) then compares it with the device clock. If the device is more than 300 s ahead, the window has already lapsed at unlock. unlock.tsx:94 calls router.replace('/(parent)/home'). useParentAccess (ui.tsx:273-276) sees the lapsed window and calls router.replace('/(parent)/unlock'). The parent is back at the PIN screen with no error. Every retry writes another server unlock.
findings.repro: The same probe (probe-skew.mts, last block) calls the real enterParentMode with a server unlockedUntil 300 s after server time and then checks parentUnlockActive at the device's time.
findings.evidence:
`parent unlock, device clock + 0 min: parentUnlockActive right after unlock = true`
`parent unlock, device clock + 6 min: parentUnlockActive right after unlock = false`
mode.ts:78 `parentUnlockedUntilMs = Number.isFinite(until) ? until : now.getTime() + 60_000;`
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the window relative to the device: store deviceNow + (unlockedUntil - serverNow), using the response Date header or an added ttlSeconds field. Clamp the result to the TTL. If the window is already over at unlock, show an error rather than redirecting silently.
findings.userImpact: A parent whose phone or tablet clock is off, often because a child changed it, cannot get into the parent area on that device at all.

findings.title: From the child space, anyone can sign the parent out with no PIN (Grown-ups, then Sign out), and doing so also takes the paired device out of child mode
findings.description: Child home's 'Grown-ups' button opens /(parent)/unlock. That screen renders SignOutButton (unlock.tsx:201) and 'Lock parent area' before any PIN is entered, because the step-up source is registered in child mode by design. signOutParent then writes mode 'signed_out' unconditionally (mode.ts:100), even on a paired device that was in child mode. Its own comment says 'A paired child device stays paired', but the device stops opening in the child space: entryRoute('signed_out', paired=true, ..., null) returns null, so every later launch shows the welcome chooser, 'I'm a parent' / 'Connect a child's device'.
findings.repro: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/mobile-r2/probe-signout.mts: real signOutParent and entryRoute, starting from mode 'child' with a stored child refresh token.
findings.evidence:
`before: mode = child | cold-start route = /(child)/home`
`  navigation -> welcome`
`after sign-out from the unlock screen: mode = signed_out | paired = true | cold-start route = null`
unlock.tsx:201 `<SignOutButton />` renders whenever `api` (the step-up client) exists, including in child mode.
findings.suggestedFix: On the unlock screen, show Sign out only after a successful unlock, or put it behind the PIN or the parental gate. In signOutParent, keep mode 'child' when the device was in child mode or holds a child pairing, and navigate to the child home instead of the welcome screen. Add a mode.test.ts case for sign-out from child mode.
findings.userImpact: A child can end the parent's session on the family tablet without the PIN. After that, the tablet opens to the parent/child chooser instead of the child's space.

findings.title: Returning from the parent area with the header back arrow or Android Back leaves a paired child device in parent mode: the next launch shows the welcome chooser, not the child's space
findings.description: Child home pushes '/(parent)/unlock', which puts the (parent) group on the root stack above (child). A successful unlock calls enterParentMode, which persists mode 'parent' and turns on screen privacy, then router.replace('/(parent)/home'). The (parent) Stack keeps the default header back button and gesture. No screen sets headerBackVisible, gestureEnabled or a BackHandler (grep finds only scan.tsx). The parent's natural way back to the child ('<' or Android/Fire Back) therefore returns to the child home without going through enterChildMode. Mode stays 'parent' in the keychain, the in-memory unlock is still live, and screen capture stays blocked in child screens. On the next cold start, entryRoute('parent', paired, …, null) returns null, so the child sees the welcome chooser instead of their space. Only the Connect-as-child-device path (pair.tsx 'Go to my space') calls enterChildMode.
findings.repro: Code path: (child)/home.tsx:122 `router.push('/(parent)/unlock')`; unlock.tsx:89-94 enterParentMode, then replace to /(parent)/home; (parent)/_layout.tsx sets no back override; entry.ts:15 returns a route for choice === null only when mode === 'child'.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'headerBackVisible|gestureEnabled|headerLeft|BackHandler' apps/mobile/app apps/mobile/src finds only app/(child)/scan.tsx:116. mode.ts:88 `await storage.setItem(STORAGE_KEYS.mode, 'parent')`; entry.ts:15 `if (choice === null) return mode === 'child' && childPaired ? '/(child)/home' : null;`
findings.suggestedFix: When a child screen gains focus, or the (child) layout mounts, while mode is 'parent', call enterChildMode. Alternatively, hide the default back on the first parent screen and give it a 'Back to child mode' button that calls enterChildMode. Either way the relock, the forgotten unlock and the persisted mode all happen.
findings.userImpact: After a parent checks something via Grown-ups and taps Back, the child's tablet no longer opens straight into the child space and keeps parent-mode settings.

findings.title: Biometric unlock keeps the parent's PIN in the keychain after sign-out and after account deletion. The next parent to sign in on the device is offered Face ID, which submits the previous parent's PIN, counts a failed attempt and shows 'Your PIN has changed'
findings.description: biometricPinStore.clear() is called only from the unlock screen's 'Turn off biometric unlock' button (unlock.tsx:178) and after a server FORBIDDEN (unlock.ts). signOutParentOnDevice (runtime.ts:161-164) and the account-closure path (privacy.tsx:146, which calls parentAuth.signOut() directly and skips signOutParentOnDevice) leave BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY and BIOMETRIC_ENABLED_KEY behind. Nothing ties the stored PIN to a user id. When a co-guardian, or a new account after deletion, signs in, isEnabled() is true and 'Unlock with Face ID or fingerprint' reads the old PIN. The server counts a wrong PIN toward the lockout, and the app says 'Your PIN has changed'. The account-closure path also leaves mode 'parent' and the in-memory unlock in place, because it bypasses signOutParent.
findings.repro: Code path: grep -rn 'biometricPinStore|BIOMETRIC_PIN_KEY' apps/mobile/app apps/mobile/src finds only unlock.tsx:59/84/119/178 and runtime.ts:61-83. There is no call from runtime.ts:161 signOutParentOnDevice, mode.ts signOutParent or privacy.tsx:146.
findings.evidence: runtime.ts:161-164 `await signOutParent(secureStorage, modeEffects, parentAuth); await forgetStoreIdentity()` (no biometric clear); privacy.tsx:146 `await parentAuth.signOut().catch(() => undefined);`
findings.suggestedFix: Call biometricPinStore.clear() in signOutParentOnDevice and in the account-closure path, and route closure through signOutParentOnDevice. Store the owning user id next to the enabled flag and ignore or clear a stored PIN that belongs to a different signed-in user.
findings.userImpact: A deleted or signed-out parent's PIN stays on the device. A second parent on a shared device gets a failing Face ID unlock that uses up a lockout attempt and shows a confusing message.

findings.title: The mobile app has no error boundary on any route, so any render-time exception takes down the whole app
findings.description: No file under apps/mobile/app or apps/mobile/src exports an expo-router ErrorBoundary, implements componentDidCatch or installs ErrorUtils.setGlobalHandler. A render error in any screen, for example from an unexpected server shape reaching a view model or a native module throwing during render, unmounts the root. In a release build that is a crash or blank screen instead of a recoverable 'Try again' view. The web portal's equivalent (WEB-R1-02) was reported and fixed; the mobile app never got one.
findings.repro: grep -rn 'ErrorBoundary|setGlobalHandler|componentDidCatch' apps/mobile/app apps/mobile/src returns nothing. I did not find a specific input that throws during render, so this is about resilience only.
findings.evidence: Empty grep output (see repro). app/_layout.tsx renders <Stack> with no boundary.
findings.suggestedFix: Export an ErrorBoundary from app/_layout.tsx, and from the (child) and (parent) layouts, that shows calm copy with a retry button (child copy: 'Something went wrong. Let's go back home.'). Add a screens.test.ts check that each layout exports one.
findings.userImpact: A single unexpected render error closes the app for a child or parent instead of showing a retry screen.

findings.title: A device that signs itself out (POST /v1/child/logout) keeps showing 'Connected' in the parent's device list
findings.description: /v1/child/logout revokes only the child_sessions row. child_devices.revoked_at stays null. GET /v1/devices (family.ts 269-296) reports status from child_devices.revoked_at alone, and the web DevicesPage renders revokedAt null as 'Status: Connected'. The mobile app calls /v1/child/logout whenever the device forgets the child (apps/mobile/src/family/child-session.ts:148-159). A logged-out tablet, or one whose 30-day session simply expired, is listed as connected for good, and each re-pair adds another 'Connected' row for the same tablet.
findings.repro: Code path: child-auth.ts:248-255 updates only public.child_sessions. family.ts:280-283 selects child_devices.revoked_at with no join to live sessions. apps/web/src/pages/app/DevicesPage.test.tsx:94 shows revokedAt null renders 'Status: Connected'.
findings.evidence: `update public.child_sessions set revoked_at = now(), revoke_reason = 'logout' where id = ${child.sessionId}` is the only write in the logout route; the devices query is `select id, child_id, label, platform, paired_at, revoked_at from public.child_devices where family_id = ...`.
findings.suggestedFix: On logout also stamp child_devices.revoked_at for the session's device when it has no other live session. Or derive the listed status from whether any live, unexpired session exists for the device, and show 'Signed out' or 'Expired' separately from 'Disconnected by you'.
findings.userImpact: Parents see stale 'Connected' devices and cannot tell which tablets can still reach their child's data.

areas.notes: IMPORTANT: these findings were NOT independently verified (the three-lens verification was skipped to save hours). For each one: reproduce it first with a failing test against the current tree; if you cannot reproduce it, change nothing for it and report it in notDone as 'not reproduced' with your evidence. Only a reproduced finding gets a fix. Every new free-text request field goes through freeTextSchema (L-028); every UI list of a contract enum reads the schema's .options (L-036); a key derived from rows a retention step can delete uses the highest kept value, never a count (L-033); a pinned clock means every fixture timestamp comes from it (L-027). Lead decisions. MOB-R2-01: one 'lock parent area' action used by backgrounding and both Lock buttons: server relock, forgetParentUnlock(), clear the parent screens' data and replace to the unlock screen; useParentAccess re-checks the unlock whenever AppState returns to 'active'; keep the Android store purchase sheet working (it backgrounds the activity) — if it would lock mid-purchase, exempt the purchase flow explicitly and test it. MOB-R2-02: the API adds an additive `accessTokenExpiresInSeconds` to the child token responses; the client stores deviceNowAtReceipt + that lifetime; on UNAUTHENTICATED with a cached access token, drop it and retry once through the EXISTING single-flight refresher in apps/mobile/src/lib/app-session.ts (never a second refresher, L-007). MOB-R2-03: the unlock response adds an additive `unlockSeconds`; the client stores deviceNow + that, clamped to it; a window already over at unlock shows an error instead of a silent redirect. MOB-R2-04: Sign out and Lock appear on the unlock screen only after a successful unlock (or behind the PIN); signOutParent keeps mode 'child' on a device that holds a child pairing and returns to the child home. MOB-R2-05: when a child screen gains focus while mode is 'parent', enter child mode (relock, forget the unlock, persist 'child'). MOB-R2-06: clear the biometric PIN store in signOutParentOnDevice and in account closure (route closure through signOutParentOnDevice), and bind the stored PIN to the user id so another user's PIN is never offered. MOB-R2-07: an expo-router ErrorBoundary on the root, (child) and (parent) layouts with calm copy and a retry. API-AUTH-R2-05: /v1/child/logout also stamps the device revoked when it has no other live session, or the device list derives 'Signed out'/'Expired' from live sessions; pick one and test it. WEB-R2-02 (web area) asks whether mobile sign-out should end only this device's session: make the mobile parent sign-out use scope 'local', so signing out of the phone never silently ends the web session; test it. Run the full apps/mobile suite, the affected API tests and both typechecks at the end.

areas.title: Web portal: sign-out, ended sessions, password change re-auth, inline step-up, page titles and focus, export link expiry, MFA kept on PIN reset, first-load fallback (WEB-R2-01,02,04..09)

findings.title: The web portal has no sign-out control; a parent on a shared or library computer stays signed in indefinitely
findings.description: The only call to auth.signOut() in apps/web/src is inside the account-closure flow (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:740). ParentNav (App.tsx:35-50), the BrandBar, RequireParent and the Security page offer no sign-out. The Supabase client uses persistSession: true and autoRefreshToken: true (supabase-auth.ts:73-80), so the session in localStorage keeps refreshing with no end. Anyone who later uses that browser can read the family's children, homework scans, verdicts, points, safety reports, devices and guardian emails, because read screens do not need the PIN. The mobile twin of this was fixed (BUG-121, MOB-R1-01). The web portal was not.
findings.repro: grep -rn "signOut" apps/web/src --include=*.tsx | grep -v test → only pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:738-740 (account closure). Probe (scratchpad web-r2/probe/session.probe.test.tsx) rendering /app pages lists buttons ['Try again'] or ['Create pairing code','Add draft child']. No sign-out exists on any page.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/App.tsx:35-50 (ParentNav has only nav links), 81-100 (Shell); apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:73-80 persistSession/autoRefreshToken; the AuthAdapter.signOut in lib/auth.ts:40 has no UI caller except PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:740.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a 'Sign out' control to the parent nav (and the admin frame). It should call POST /v1/adult/lock while the token is valid, then auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }), then navigate to /sign-in. Show 'Signed in as p•••@…' next to it. Add a test that every /app page exposes sign-out and that it clears the session.
findings.userImpact: A parent who uses a shared family, school or library computer cannot end the session. Their children's homework and results stay readable by whoever uses the browser next.

findings.area: web portal / expired or ended session
findings.title: A session the server has ended leaves every portal page on 'Sign in again to continue' + 'Try again' with no sign-in link, for up to about an hour
findings.description: useParentSession only reacts to onAuthStateChange. auth.getSession() returns the stored access token until it is about 90 s from expiry (supabase auth-js EXPIRY_MARGIN_MS = 3 × 30 s). When the server ends the session, the portal still believes it is signed in. That happens when the parent signs out in the mobile app: parent-auth.ts:107 calls client.auth.signOut() with no scope, and supabase-js defaults to scope 'global' (GoTrueClient.js:3409), which ends every session of that user, the web one included. It also happens after a password change elsewhere and after the account-closure revocation. The API then answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED 'Sign in again to continue' (api/src/auth/parent.ts:147). The page shows that text in an ErrorState whose only action is 'Try again', which fails again. The page has no sign-in link, and the portal has no sign-out (WEB-R2-01) that could clear the dead local session. The parent is stuck until the JWT expires, which takes up to 1 h with default settings.
findings.repro: Probe test (scratchpad hardening/web-r2/probe/session.probe.test.tsx) renders FamilyDashboardPage with a signed-in adapter and an API that rejects with ApiRequestError('UNAUTHENTICATED','Sign in again to continue',401). Output: links: [] buttons: ["Try again"]. The test passed, confirming no link to /sign-in. Supabase default scope: grep -n 'async signOut' node_modules/.pnpm/@supabase+auth-js@2.116.0/.../GoTrueClient.js → 3409: async signOut(options = { scope: 'global' }).
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/lib/session.tsx:45-66 (state from getSession/onChange only), 111-137 (useApiQuery never reacts to UNAUTHENTICATED); apps/mobile/src/lib/parent-auth.ts:106-107; apps/api/src/auth/parent.ts:106-147.
findings.suggestedFix: In useApiQuery (or a wrapper around the API client), treat code UNAUTHENTICATED on a parent call as signed out: call auth.signOut({ scope: 'local' }) and let RequireParent render the SignInPrompt, keeping ?next=. Decide whether mobile sign-out should be scope 'local' so that signing out of the phone does not silently end the web session. Add a regression test with a 401 from /v1/family.
findings.userImpact: After signing out of the phone app, a parent who opens the portal sees 'Sign in again to continue' on every page with no way to sign in except typing /sign-in by hand.

findings.title: /update-password changes the account password from any signed-in session with no current password or re-authentication
findings.description: When the page is opened without a recovery link (recovery.status === 'none') and a session exists, it renders the 'Choose a new password' form. updatePassword calls auth.updateUser({ password }) with no nonce and no check of the current password (supabase-auth.ts:118-123). The weaker secret is protected more strongly: resetting the 6-digit PIN needs the account password re-proved within 10 minutes (PinResetPage.tsx:33, adult.ts:77-88). Combined with WEB-R2-01, anyone at a browser the parent once used can open /update-password, set a new password, and so take over the account, including the ability to request exports and deletions after a PIN reset. Supabase then ends the parent's other sessions. Whether the hosted project enforces 'Secure password change' (reauthentication) is not in the repo (no supabase/config.toml), so the server-side half is a candidate.
findings.repro: Code path: UpdatePasswordPage.tsx:71-86 falls through to AccountForm when state.status === 'signed_in' and there is no recovery link. onSubmit calls account.updatePassword(password) (line 99) → supabase-auth.ts:118-123 auth.updateUser({ password }) with no nonce. Existing web test 'UpdatePasswordPage' renders the form for a signed-in adapter. No repo file configures secure_password_change (ls supabase → migrations node_modules package.json scripts tests tsconfig.json vitest.config.ts).
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/pages/auth/UpdatePasswordPage.tsx:71-100; apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:118-123; apps/web/src/pages/app/PinResetPage.tsx:27-35 (re-auth required for the PIN only).
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the direct form only right after a recovery link (a PASSWORD_RECOVERY event or amr containing recovery/otp within a short window). Otherwise ask for the current password (signInWithPassword) or use auth.reauthenticate() and pass the nonce to updateUser. Record 'Secure password change' ON as an owner action for the hosted project.
findings.userImpact: An unattended signed-in browser is enough to take over a parent account and lock the parent out of their other devices.

findings.title: Every step-up refusal outside the privacy page sends the parent to /app/security, losing the form they were filling, with no way back
findings.description: StepUpNotice (SecurityPage.tsx:63-72, duplicated in HomeworkPage.tsx:228-237) is the only step-up path on the Children, Guardians, Devices, Family (consent withdraw, create family), Rewards, Homework and Support pages. It links to /app/security and says 'then try again'. Following the link unmounts the page, so a typed child nickname, guardian email or support message is lost. The Security page has no link back to where the parent was. Only PrivacyControlsPage has an inline PIN prompt (StepUpPrompt, lines 186-282). Nearly every parent hits this the first time they add a child, invite a guardian or approve a reward, because an unlock lasts only a few minutes.
findings.repro: ChildrenPage AddChildForm: type 'Riley', submit with no recent unlock → API STEP_UP_REQUIRED → ActionFeedback renders StepUpNotice (SecurityPage.tsx:89) → the link goes to /app/security. Returning to /app/children re-renders AddChildForm with an empty nickname (state is local to the unmounted component, ChildrenPage.tsx:297-300).
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/pages/app/SecurityPage.tsx:63-90; apps/web/src/pages/app/HomeworkPage.tsx:228-251; apps/web/src/pages/app/PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:186 (the inline prompt exists but is not shared).
findings.suggestedFix: Reuse PrivacyControlsPage's inline StepUpPrompt in the shared ActionFeedback, so the PIN is entered in place and the action is retried. At minimum, link to /app/security?next=<current path> and return after unlocking.

findings.title: Portal, admin and auth pages never set a page title and do not move focus or scroll on client-side navigation; signed-out /app pages have no h1
findings.description: Only public pages set document.title (pages/public/common.tsx:114-123). findings.title: Re-proving the password for a PIN reset replaces the session with a new aal1 one, silently dropping an owner's MFA (aal2) admin access
findings.description: PinReset's 'Confirm it's you' step calls account.signInWithPassword(email, password). That creates a new Supabase session at aal1 and replaces the stored one. For the owner-admin, the aal2 session obtained on /admin/mfa is gone, and every /admin page falls back to 'Owner administration requires an MFA session' until TOTP is entered again. The old session is also not signed out on the server. The portal says nothing about either.
findings.repro: Code path: PinResetPage.tsx:30-35 → supabase-auth.ts:88-99 auth.signInWithPassword (password grant → aal1). admin-ui.tsx:31/41-52 renders AdminAccessDenied for the resulting FORBIDDEN.
findings.evidence: apps/web/src/pages/app/PinResetPage.tsx:27-35; apps/web/src/lib/supabase-auth.ts:88-99; apps/web/src/pages/admin/components/admin-ui.tsx:31-52.
findings.suggestedFix: Re-prove with auth.reauthenticate() (nonce) or verify the password without replacing the session. If a new session is unavoidable, send the owner to /admin/mfa afterwards and sign the previous session out.
findings.userImpact: The owner loses admin access unexpectedly after resetting the PIN.

findings.area: web portal / family and child management
findings.title: No client can change a child's grade, nickname or age band, the family's name or time zone, or archive a child. The archive API has no caller, yet the app tells parents to 'archive them in Children'
findings.description: ChildCard offers only 'Create pairing code' (active) or 'Assign an unused paid slot' (draft). The web and mobile clients send no PATCH or PUT to /v1/family or /v1/children/:id. The only PATCH/PUT calls are for promo templates, the learning schedule and the PIN. The API has no route to update a child or family profile at all. POST /v1/children/:childId/archive exists (api/src/routes/family.ts:236) but no client calls it. The mobile plan screen tells parents 'To stop a child's paid features sooner, archive them in Children' (apps/mobile/app/(parent)/plan.tsx:453), and no Children screen offers that. The grade drives practice generation (learning-jobs.ts:245 bankGrade(child.grade_level); learning.ts:927 bankCoverage(owned.gradeLevel)). When the school year rolls over, every child keeps last year's grade. The only workaround is 'Delete a child's data' on the privacy page, which destroys the child's history, points and rewards and needs a fresh profile, slot assignment and pairing. The family time zone is a free-text field that defaults to the browser zone at creation (FamilyDashboardPage.tsx:340-347) and can never be corrected afterwards.
findings.repro: Probe test (scratchpad hardening/web-r2/probe/session.probe.test.tsx) rendering ChildrenPage with Riley (active, grade 3) and Sam (draft), all slots used. Output: buttons: ["Create pairing code","Add draft child"]. The test passed, confirming no archive, edit or grade control. grep of client PATCH/PUT calls (apps/web/src, apps/mobile/src, apps/mobile/app) → only /v1/admin/promo-templates, the learning schedule and /v1/adult/pin. grep '/archive' in both clients → no caller.
findings.evidence: apps/api/src/routes/family.ts:35-270 (POST families/children/pairing-code/activate/archive only; no PATCH); apps/mobile/app/(parent)/plan.tsx:453; apps/api/src/jobs/learning-jobs.ts:216-245; apps/web/src/pages/app/ChildrenPage.tsx:130-257.
findings.suggestedFix: Add PATCH /v1/children/:id (nickname, gradeLevel 0-8, ageBand; step-up) and PATCH /v1/family (displayName, timezone validated as IANA; step-up), with contracts and tests. Add Edit and 'Archive (keeps history, frees the slot)' actions to the web Children page and the mobile Children screen, wired to the existing archive route. Until then, remove the 'archive them in Children' copy.
findings.userImpact: Every family's practice is pitched at the wrong grade after the school year changes. A family cannot free a paid slot or fix a typo in a name or time zone without deleting the child's whole history.

findings.title: A child whose data deletion is pending can be re-activated, paired and used to collect new homework until the purge runs
findings.description: request_deletion archives the child, revokes sessions and devices and marks scans deleted. POST /v1/children/:childId/activate (family.ts 191-233) accepts any non-active child: it checks consent and a free slot, then sets status = 'active', with no deletion_requests check. POST /children/:childId/pairing-code (128-188) checks only status = 'active' and consent, and /v1/child/pair only checks the claimed child is active. After re-activation the child pairs a new device and starts new scans while the deletion is still 'requested'. This breaks spec P4 ('deletion requests should stop processing immediately'), which the learning, rewards and export routes all enforce with their deletion-pending checks. The purge then deletes the re-activated profile and everything added since, without warning. If the purge keeps failing (the already-reported dead-letter after about 5 attempts), the child stays usable indefinitely under an open deletion request. GET /v1/family also still lists the child under deletion as 'archived'. The portal and app only offer 'Assign a slot' for drafts, so the path is a direct API call, a guardian acting in parallel, or a future UI change.
findings.repro: Probe: <scratch>/hardening/api-auth/reactivate.probe.ts. Run: `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.config.mts --reporter=default reactivate` from apps/api.
findings.evidence: `PROBE deletion 202 ... status requested` / `PROBE sam status after deletion request archived` / `PROBE activate during pending deletion 200 {"status":"active",...}` / `PROBE pairing code during pending deletion 201` / `PROBE pair 201` / `PROBE child creates scan during pending deletion 201 {"assignment":{..."status":"draft"...}}` / `PROBE family children ["active","active"]` / then `PROBE runJobs {"succeeded":1}` and `PROBE after purge: profile rows 0 ... deletion completed`: the re-activated child and its new scan are removed without notice.
findings.suggestedFix: In activate and pairing-code (and, defensively, the /pair claim and resolveCaller's child branch), refuse a child with a deletion_requests row in ('requested','processing') using the same NOT_FOUND or business rule as ownedChild(). A database backstop is better still: a trigger that refuses status -> 'active' while such a request is open. Leave children under deletion out of GET /v1/family, as the other parent reads already do.
findings.userImpact: New data about the child is collected after the parent asked for it to be deleted. A parent who thinks 'activate' restores the child loses that profile and its new homework when the purge runs.

findings.title: Calendar dates in year 0000 pass the contract and answer 500 on test-date and learning-schedule writes
findings.description: calendarDateSchema = z.iso.date() accepts '0000-01-01' because the year part is any \d{4}. Postgres has no year 0, so the `::date` casts in POST /v1/children/:childId/test-dates (learning.ts 759-803) and PUT /v1/children/:childId/learning-schedule (pause.from/to, learning.ts 681-736) raise 22008. That SQLSTATE is not in knownConstraintError, so it surfaces as an unhandled 500 and an error log. The contract also has no plausibility bounds: test dates in 0001, 1900 and 9999 are stored and listed. calendarMonthSchema (^\d{4}-...) likely has the same year-0000 hole on the admin month parameters that go through monthToDate(); that is labelled a candidate because it was not probed.
findings.repro: Probe: <scratch>/hardening/api-auth/dates.probe.ts. Run: `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.config.mts --reporter=default dates` from apps/api.
findings.evidence: `PROBE test-date 0000-01-01: 500 {"error":{"code":"INTERNAL",...}}`; `PROBE schedule pause {"from":"0000-01-01","to":"0000-01-02"}: 500 INTERNAL`; `LOGS [{"level":"error","event":"unhandled_error",...,"code":"PostgresError"} x2]`; `PROBE test-date 0001-01-01: 201`, `9999-12-31: 201`, `1900-01-01: 201`.
findings.suggestedFix: Bound calendarDateSchema (and calendarMonthSchema) to a sane range, for example years 2000-2100, or refine against a window around `now` for test dates. Also map 22008/22007/22003 (datetime/numeric out of range) to VALIDATION_FAILED in knownConstraintError, as was done for 22021.
findings.userImpact: A typo in a year field gives a generic 'Something went wrong' instead of a validation message, and implausible dates are saved.

findings.title: Parent practice sets (30), safety reports (100), exports (100) and promotions (100) are hard-capped with no cursor
findings.description: The earlier fix added keyset cursors to the homework list and points history only. GET /v1/children/:childId/practice-sets returns `limit ${PARENT_SET_LIMIT}` (30, learning.ts line 109) ordered by created_at desc, with no cursor or date filter. A child gets a daily set every day, so after about a month older daily sets cannot be listed. Their ids are needed for GET /v1/practice-sets/:id/answer-key and POST /v1/exports/review-pdf, so the parent can no longer open or print those answer keys. GET /v1/safety-reports (privacy.ts 729-746, limit 100) is capped the same way: under the owner decision every flag goes to the parent for action, yet a flag older than the newest 100 reports cannot be seen or resolved from the list. GET /v1/exports (privacy.ts 660-672) and GET /v1/family/promotions (promotions.ts 474-486) are also capped at 100 with no cursor.
findings.repro: Code path: learning.ts:109 `const PARENT_SET_LIMIT = 30;`; learning.ts:986 `limit ${PARENT_SET_LIMIT}` with no `after`/`before` parameter; privacy.ts:740 `order by created_at desc limit 100`; privacy.ts:667 `limit 100`; promotions.ts:482 `limit 100`. The web PracticeSetsSection (apps/web/src/components/learning/PracticeSetsSection.tsx:66-69) sends only `?kind=`.
findings.evidence: Contracts practiceSetsResponseSchema and the safety-report and exports list schemas have no nextCursor field. The web client requests `/v1/children/{id}/practice-sets` and optionally `?kind=`, with no paging.
findings.suggestedFix: Add keyset cursors (created_at micros plus id, parsed with the existing cursorMicros helper) to practice sets and safety reports, or at least an explicit 'open reports first' ordering so unresolved flags are never cut off. Add a date or week filter for daily sets so older answer keys can be reached.
findings.userImpact: After a few weeks a parent cannot reach older daily practice sets or their answer keys. In a heavy-flag family an old unresolved safety flag drops out of the list.

findings.title: Clearing a flag as a false alarm answers 409 and rolls back once job retention has pruned an earlier scan job
findings.description: queueClearanceRecheck, which both the parent's 'This was a false alarm' action and the admin clearing path use, still builds the next scan job key from a COUNT of the kept `scan:<id>:v%` rows: `select count(*)::int as n from public.jobs ... idempotency_key like 'scan:<id>:v%'` and then inserts `scan:<id>:v${n+1}` with no `on conflict`. Since BUG-139, app.prune_terminal_jobs deletes terminal jobs older than 90 days. So once v1 has been pruned while a later v2 is still kept, the count is 1 and the new key is v2 again. The insert raises 23505, app.onError maps it to 409 'This was already done', and the whole transaction rolls back: the report stays escalated, the child's notice stays and nothing is graded. homework.ts was changed to use max(version) (lines 1016-1020 and 1386-1390, with a comment naming this exact hazard). privacy.ts:414 was not changed, and the dispatcher comment at lines 1217-1221 still assumes the count.
findings.repro: Probe (scratchpad, not in the repo): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/safety-r2/probe-clear.test.ts. Run it with `cd apps/api && npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.probe.config.mjs --reporter=default probe-clear`. Steps: (1) the flaggedFamily fixture from parent-flag-review.test.ts produces a flagged scan (v1 succeeded). (2) v1's updated_at is aged to 100 days with triggers off, as job-retention.review.test.ts does, and a v2 'succeeded' recheck from 10 days ago is added, standing in for an earlier parent correction. (3) select app.prune_terminal_jobs('90 days'). (4) PATCH /v1/safety-reports/:id {outcome:'false_match'} with an unlocked parent.
findings.evidence: Probe output: `PROBE kept keys: ["scan:e84a...:v2"]`, `PROBE PATCH status: 409 {"error":{"code":"CONFLICT","message":"This was already done"...}}`, `PROBE report after PATCH: {"status":"escalated","resolution":null}`. Code: privacy.ts:413-421 (count, then insert without on conflict). homework.ts:1015-1020 has the fixed max() form.
findings.suggestedFix: Use the same `coalesce(max(substring(idempotency_key from ':v([0-9]+)$')::int), 0)` as homework.ts in queueClearanceRecheck, and add a regression test in which v1 is pruned and v2 is kept, for both PATCH /v1/safety-reports/:id and PATCH /v1/admin/safety-reports/:id. Also correct the dispatcher.ts:1217-1221 comment.
findings.userImpact: A parent, or the owner's reviewer, cannot clear a false alarm on an older scan that was re-checked in the last 90 days. The only feedback is a confusing 'This was already done', and the child keeps the safety notice with no hints on that question.

findings.title: A provider flag with no mapped category (flagged:true with no category, a new or unknown category, harassment/hate/illicit) is graded and coached with no notice, no report and no parent email
findings.description: On the child's answers, childInputScreen (scan-process.ts:545-558) uses providerSafetyScreen, which is severe only when a category maps to a PencilLift category. `if (!isOpenAiCategory(category)) continue;` drops any category name not in the fixed 2024 list, and harassment/hate/illicit map to null (lines 106-108). An input the provider reports as `flagged: true` with no category, or only with a category added later, therefore reads as level 'none'. The answer is sent to grading, verification and coaching, and the only trace is a warn log 'moderation_flag_child_input'. This contradicts the comment on moderationFlagged ('fails closed on categories', line 144) and the owner decision that every flag goes to the parent. Model output is moderated with moderationFlagged, which does fail closed, so only the child-input path is open. harassment on its own is covered by a test as 'only logs' (provider-moderation.test.ts:484), so that sub-case is a candidate owner decision. The uncategorized and unknown-category cases have no test.
findings.repro: (a) `npx tsx <scratch>/probe-mod.mts`: providerSafetyScreen({flagged:true,categories:[]}) -> none; ['self-harm/new-subcategory'] -> none; ['illicit'] -> none; ['self-harm/intent'] -> severe. (b) End to end: <scratch>/probe-audit.test.ts, test 'flagged:true with no category'. The scripted labeled mock moderation returns {flagged:true, categories:[]} for one answer, and the scan job runs.
findings.evidence: Probe output: `PROBE reports: 0 feedback kinds: ["method_step","hint","encouragement"] model stages that received the flagged answer: ["private_grading","independent_verification","child_coaching_packet"] email jobs: 0`, with only the log `{"event":"moderation_flag_child_input","code":"PROVIDER_FLAGGED"}`.
findings.suggestedFix: For child input, when moderationFlagged(item) is true and no category maps, treat the input as severe with a fallback report category (for example, the child gets the generic safety template and the parent gets a flag), or at least fail closed for flagged-without-category and unknown categories. Ask the owner whether harassment/hate/illicit on a child's own answer should also reach the parent under the 2026-09-25 decision. Add scan-level tests.
findings.userImpact: A child's answer that the provider moderation flags can get AI hints, and the parent is never told, when the provider reports the flag without one of the currently mapped categories.

findings.title: Withdrawing consent while a recheck is queued leaves the scan in 'checking' forever; the flag can then never be cleared and the child never sees that scan's results again, even after consent is given again
findings.description: POST /v1/consent/withdraw cancels every queued or failed_retryable job not on the keep-list, scan_process included, but leaves the assignments as they are. A recheck (queued by a false-alarm clearance, privacy.ts:409-421, or by a transcription correction) has already moved the scan to 'checking', and nothing moves it back. No sweep recovers a 'checking' scan with no live job, and a new consent re-queues nothing. From then on: cancel refuses ('checking' is not in CANCELLABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES), correction refuses (CORRECTABLE statuses), clearing any other flag on that scan refuses with SCAN_STILL_CHECKING (privacy.ts:385), and the child's results for the whole scan stay hidden (RESULT_VISIBLE_STATUSES = ready, needs_parent_review; homework.ts:159). The same withdrawal also leaves an initial scan 'queued' with its usage reservation held, although that one can be cancelled. This is a different defect from the reported 'consent withdrawal leaves the child operational' and 'withdrawal cancels the flag email' (BUG-136/137).
findings.repro: Probe: <scratch>/probe-withdraw.test.ts. Steps: flagged scan; PATCH false_match (status -> checking, v2 queued); POST /v1/consent/withdraw; insert a new verified consent record; runJobs now and again 7 days later; then try to cancel and to correct.
findings.evidence: `PROBE status after clearing: checking`, `PROBE withdraw: 200 {"state":"withdrawn","cancelledJobs":1}`, `PROBE runJobs a week later: {"succeeded":0,...}`, `PROBE assignment status a week later: checking jobs: [v1 succeeded, v2 cancelled]`, `PROBE cancel scan: 422 ... INVALID_TRANSITION`, `PROBE correction: 422 ... This scan is still being checked`.
findings.suggestedFix: In the same withdrawal transaction, settle every scan whose scan_process job was cancelled. A recheck should go back to the pre-recheck state (needs_parent_review keeps results), and a queued initial scan should become cancelled with its reservation released. Alternatively, re-queue those scans when consent is verified again. Add a 'checking with no live job' recovery sweep and a regression test.
findings.userImpact: A scan's results disappear for the child for good, and the parent loses every action on that scan (clear flag, correct, cancel).

findings.title: Consent withdrawal cancels queued scan jobs but leaves their scans 'queued' or 'checking' for good: a re-check stays 'checking' forever and cannot be corrected or cancelled; queued scans keep their allowance reserved
findings.description: POST /v1/consent/withdraw cancels every queued or failed_retryable job whose kind is not in JOBS_KEPT_ON_CONSENT_WITHDRAWAL, and scan_process is not in that list. It does not touch the assignments those jobs belonged to. A scan that is *running* at the moment of withdrawal is settled correctly: assertActive throws CONSENT_REQUIRED, the scan goes to failed_final and the reservation is released. A scan that is merely queued is stranded. After a parent correction the scan sits in 'checking' (the recheck job was cancelled). 'checking' is neither in CANCELLABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES nor in CORRECTABLE_ASSIGNMENT_STATUSES, so the scan can never leave that state, even after consent is given again. A finalized scan sits in 'queued' with its usage_reservations row still 'reserved', which counts against the month's page allowance. Nothing re-enqueues either job after re-consent.
findings.repro: Probe: scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/consent-strand.probe.test.ts. Consented family with active child Riley. Scan A: ready, then POST /v1/questions/:id/correction (moves to 'checking' with a queued recheck job). Scan B: queued with a reserved reservation and a queued initial job. POST /v1/consent/withdraw, insert a new verified consent, run jobs for 3 days. Then correct A again and cancel A.
findings.evidence: Output: `correction 200`, `withdraw 200`, `3 days later: scan A checking | scan B queued | jobs [["v1","cancelled","consent_withdrawn"],["v1","cancelled","consent_withdrawn"]] | reservation B reserved | correcting A again -> 422 {"rule":"INVALID_TRANSITION","message":"This scan is still being checked. Try again when it is ready."} | cancelling A -> 422`.
findings.suggestedFix: In the same withdrawal transaction, settle the assignments behind the cancelled scan jobs as the running path does: initial scans in queued or failed_retryable go to failed_final with CONSENT_REQUIRED and their reservations are released; rechecks in checking or verifying go to needs_parent_review. Alternatively, keep scan_process jobs and let the handler's CONSENT_REQUIRED path settle them. Add a regression test that asserts the assignment state after withdrawal.
findings.userImpact: The parent's corrected scan shows 'still being checked' forever and can never be corrected again. Queued scans spin indefinitely and eat into the month's page allowance.

findings.title: The parent's safety-report list (and the exports list) is hard-capped at the newest 100 rows with no cursor
findings.description: GET /v1/safety-reports selects `... where family_id = $1 order by created_at desc limit 100` and GET /v1/exports does the same (line 667). There is no nextCursor. Once a family has more than 100 reports, which frequent word-list false matches, child reports and parent reports can produce, older unresolved flags cannot be reached in the portal or the app, so the parent cannot mark them looked into or clear them. BUG-117 fixed the same shape for assignments and points history only.
findings.repro: Read privacy.ts:733-739 and 663-668. The contracts' safetyReportsResponseSchema has no cursor field.
findings.evidence: privacy.ts:737 `order by created_at desc limit 100`; privacy.ts:667 the same on data_exports.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply BUG-117's keyset pattern (after=<micros>_<id>, nextCursor), or list unresolved reports first, without a cap.
findings.userImpact: Older open flags silently drop off the parent's list.

findings.title: An export whose upload landed but whose answer was lost ends 'failed' with its file orphaned in storage; the family deletion purge never removes it
findings.description: storageUploader PUTs through a signed upload URL that Supabase signs with x-upsert:false (supabase-storage.ts:175). If the first PUT stores the object but the Worker never sees the answer (the 20 s AbortSignal.timeout on a large family_data JSON, a connection reset, the worker killed, or the following `update data_exports set status='ready'` failing), every retry PUTs to the same deterministic path `exports/{family}/{id}.{ext}` and is refused as a duplicate. On the final attempt the handler calls markFailed('UPLOAD_FAILED') (line 531): the row becomes status 'failed' with storage_path null. The deletion purge (dispatcher.ts:238-244) only removes `storage_path` values and the deterministic paths of *queued* exports, so the orphaned object (whole-family JSON with every child's records, or an answer key) is never removed: not by the family deletion, not by the 7-day expiry sweep (which only reads status 'ready'). Threat_Model T26 claims 'orphaned export' is mitigated. Secondary: the ledger records last_error_code 'Error' for these failures (plain Error, not a JobFailure code; the BUG-159 fix did not reach export_build).
findings.repro: Probe (labeled mocks, synthetic family): scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/export-orphan.probe.test.ts. It uses the real storageUploader with a fake fetch that emulates Supabase x-upsert:false. The first PUT stores the object and then throws a TimeoutError; later PUTs get HTTP 400 'Duplicate'. Then POST /v1/exports {kind:'family_data'}, 8 runJobs ticks, POST /v1/deletion {scope:'family'} and 3 purge ticks. Run: copy the probe and probe-config.ts into apps/api/node_modules/.probes, then `npx vitest run --config node_modules/.probe-config.ts export-orphan`.
findings.evidence: Output: `export row {"status":"failed","storage_path":null} job {"status":"succeeded","attempts":5,"last_error_code":"Error"} puts 5 stored objects ['exports/1028d648-.../2680897e-....json']`, then `deletion status 202`, `purge tick 0 {"succeeded":1,...}`, `paths removed by the purge []`, `orphan removed? false`.
findings.suggestedFix: Treat a duplicate (400/409 'already exists') on retry as success when the stored object's size or hash matches the bytes built, or upload with upsert for this job-owned path. In the deletion purge, also remove the deterministic `exports/{family}/{id}.{ext}` paths for exports in any non-ready state ('failed', and 'queued' as today). Add a regression test for 'upload stored, answer lost, then retry'. Give export failures JobFailure codes.
findings.userImpact: A parent who deletes the family (COPPA deletion) leaves a complete copy of the children's data, or an answer key, in private storage indefinitely. The parent also sees 'failed' for an export whose file exists.

findings.title: A provider answer cut off at max_output_tokens ('incomplete') is re-sent unchanged: 10 billed calls, then failed_final. A 50-problem math-facts sheet cannot fit the 4,000-token extraction budget
findings.description: runStage treats `response.kind === 'incomplete'` (reason max_output_tokens) like a transient provider failure: lastError = 'PROVIDER_FAILED', then it retries the identical request with the identical maxOutputTokens. scan-process.ts:1157 turns that into RetryableFailure('EXTRACTION_PROVIDER_FAILED' or 'GRADING_PROVIDER_FAILED'), so the job retries it up to max_attempts (5). The output budget is 4,000 tokens for extraction and for grading (routing.ts PROPOSED_STAGE_LIMITS), and reasoning tokens count against it too. Nothing splits the work (per page, per question batch) and nothing caps the number of questions. By my estimate (JSON chars/3.2), a single-page sheet of 50 one-line multiplication facts already needs about 4,100 extraction output tokens, and 60 need about 5,000. Timed-facts sheets of 50 to 100 problems are routine in grades 2 to 4, and multi-page scans of up to 10 pages multiply this. Such a scan can never succeed, but it is billed on every attempt and ends failed_final with a code that reads like an outage.
findings.repro: Probe: scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/incomplete.probe.test.ts. The labeled mock Responses client answers every call with {kind:'incomplete', reason:'max_output_tokens', usage 1,800 in / 4,000 out}. One queued 1-page scan, 8 runJobs ticks, 7 h apart. Run via the probe config: `npx vitest run --config node_modules/.probe-config.ts incomplete`.
findings.evidence: Output: ticks 0-3 `failed_retryable EXTRACTION_PROVIDER_FAILED`, tick 4 `failed_final EXTRACTION_PROVIDER_FAILED`, then `provider calls 10 metered rows 10 micros 516000 max_output_tokens sent [ 4000 ]`. Size estimate: node script, 50 fact questions = 13,231 chars (about 4,135 tokens), 60 = 15,907 chars (about 4,971 tokens), 100 = 26,620 chars (about 8,319 tokens). The token counts are approximate; the retry-unchanged path is exact.
findings.suggestedFix: Give max_output_tokens incompletes their own error code (e.g. OUTPUT_TRUNCATED) and do not retry them identically. Split extraction per page and grading into question batches, or raise the budget for the retry within the stage cost cap. If the work still cannot fit, end the scan with a parent-facing code such as SCAN_TOO_MANY_QUESTIONS (send it to parent review or ask for fewer pages) instead of 5 job attempts. Cap the questions per scan in the extraction prompt or schema.
findings.userImpact: Children who scan an ordinary long worksheet get a failed check after a long wait, and the owner pays for 10 or more wasted model calls per such scan.

findings.title: export_build has no dead-letter compensation: an export whose final attempt dies (lease expiry, or any error outside build/upload) stays 'queued' forever
findings.description: exportBuildHandler is a plain function with no onDeadLetter (compare safetyFlagEmailHandler, the scan handler, deletion_purge and account_close). The handler marks the row failed only on the final attempt and only for errors from build() and upload(). If the final attempt's worker dies (LOCK_EXPIRED recovery dead-letters the job), or the final `update ... set status='ready'` or markFailed itself throws, compensateDeadLetter finds nothing to call. The data_exports row stays 'queued'; purgeExpiredExports only reads 'ready' rows, and nothing else ever moves it.
findings.repro: Probe: scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/export-dead.probe.test.ts. POST /v1/exports {kind:'progress_csv'}, then mark its job running with attempts = max_attempts and an expired lease (a worker killed on the final attempt), runJobs, advance 30 days, runJobs, GET /v1/exports.
findings.evidence: Output: `report {"succeeded":0,"retried":0,"deadLettered":1} | job {"status":"dead_letter","last_error_code":"LOCK_EXPIRED"} | export row 30 days later {"status":"queued"} | portal list shows {..., "status":"queued", "expiresAt":null}`.
findings.suggestedFix: Give exportBuildHandler an onDeadLetter that marks the row 'failed' when it is still 'queued', and that also removes the deterministic export path (see JOBS-R2-01).
findings.userImpact: The parent's export list shows 'preparing' forever for that export.

findings.title: A scan paused at the spend ceiling re-downloads and re-encodes every page each hour before it is refused again (288 MiB a day for one 12 MiB scan)
findings.description: ScanRun.extract() reads each page from storage, hashes it, strips its metadata and base64-encodes it (lines 1231-1265) before this.spending(['extraction']) asks for a spend hold (line 1267). When the hold is refused, pause() defers the job by 1 hour without spending an attempt, and the next run repeats the full read. The same happens in staging and production for every scan while the month has no budget row (SpendBudgetMissing, LJA-F2). Paused scans are also claimed by every tick alongside deletion purges and safety emails. There is no upper bound on how long a scan stays paused.
findings.repro: Probe: scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/pause-reads.probe.test.ts. A 2026-09 budget of 1 micro, one queued 4-page scan (about 3 MiB per page), 24 runJobs ticks 61 minutes apart.
findings.evidence: Output: `after 24 hourly pauses: {"status":"failed_retryable","error_code":"SPEND_CEILING","processing_attempts":24} {"status":"failed_retryable","attempts":0} | page reads 96 | MiB read 288.0 | AI calls 0`.
findings.suggestedFix: Check admission, or a cheap pre-check of the ceiling (acquire the hold) before reading any page, then read and encode the pages inside the admitted window. Consider a growing pause interval and a maximum pause after which the scan settles with a parent-visible state.
findings.userImpact: Storage egress and Worker time are wasted for as long as the ceiling holds, and the child's scan stays 'being checked' with no end.

findings.title: candidate: the 10-minute claim budget is measured from runJobs' own start, after unbounded earlier steps, so a job can be claimed moments before the invocation's wall limit and killed mid-run
findings.description: runJobs sets `started = deps.clock()` (line 639) and stops claiming once 10 minutes have passed since then (lines 69, 670). The doc comment says the budget exists because a Cron invocation lives at most 15 minutes of wall time (line 64). Every step before the ledger is unbounded in time. The inactivity sweep sends up to 50 emails with a 10 s timeout each (about 8 minutes in an email outage). Up to 25 entitlement syncs go to RevenueCat with no timeout (JOBS-R2-04). Storage removals run too. The ledger can therefore start late and claim a new job at, say, minute 14. That job then has no time to finish. The kill spends an attempt, and the job stays invisible until its 20-minute lease expires. A long scan (sequential coaching calls of up to 2 x 45 s per incorrect question) is the most exposed. The platform limit could not be verified: developers.cloudflare.com returned a proxy 403.
findings.repro: Code path: dispatcher.ts:639 (started), :670 (budget check), :1172-1236 (steps that run before 'jobs' at :1237), :1057-1060 (inactivity notices sent in sequence), :900-919 (entitlement syncs in sequence).
findings.evidence: curl https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/ gave `CONNECT tunnel failed, response 403`. The 15-minute figure is the repository's own statement at dispatcher.ts:64.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass the tick start into runJobs and measure the claim budget from it. Before claiming, also require enough remaining time for the job kind's expected worst case (e.g. no new scan_process claim after minute 8).
findings.userImpact: Occasional scans and deletions are delayed by 20 minutes or more, and each kill spends one of the job's five attempts.

findings.title: candidate: server-side metadata stripping drops the JPEG EXIF Orientation along with APP1, so a photo that relied on it reaches the model sideways and may be sent back for a retake as 'rotated'
findings.description: stripJpeg keeps an allow-list (JFIF, ICC, tables, frame, scans) and drops every APP1 segment, including the EXIF Orientation tag, without applying the rotation to the pixels. The mobile app (native-io.ts normalizePhoto) and the web portal (image-downscale.ts) usually re-encode with the orientation applied. Both fall back to uploading the original file when that step fails (normalizePhoto's doc comment and downscaleForUpload's `return file` paths). For such files the extraction model receives the sensor-oriented image. RESCAN_PAGE_ISSUES includes 'rotated', so the scan goes to needs_rescan, and a retake on the same device fails the same way.
findings.repro: Code path: image-metadata.ts:196-205 (only JFIF, ICC, tables and frame are kept; APP1 is dropped), scan-process.ts:148 (a 'rotated' page issue means rescan), apps/web/src/lib/image-downscale.ts:105-133 and apps/mobile/src/homework/native-io.ts:74-90 (fallback to the original file). Not probed end to end: no real provider is available.
findings.evidence: Header comment at image-metadata.ts:9: 'Everything else is dropped: APP1 (Exif, GPS, XMP)'. No code reads the Orientation tag.
findings.suggestedFix: Read the EXIF Orientation (tag 0x0112) before dropping APP1. Either re-emit a minimal APP1 containing only Orientation, or pass the rotation to the model as page metadata in the data envelope.
findings.userImpact: On a device whose re-encode step fails, a portrait photo is sent sideways and the child may be asked to retake it repeatedly.

findings.area: child safety / privacy of flag category
findings.title: Every family member can read a flag's provider category codes (e.g. PROVIDER_SELF_HARM_INTENT) from the audit log through the Data API
findings.description: The design keeps the kind of concern away from the family. screen_categories is not granted to `authenticated` (0760 section 5). The API says 'the family sees that an answer was flagged for a grown-up, never which kind of concern' (privacy.ts:720-724), and the flag email names 'no kind of concern'. However, safetyResponse writes an audit_events row with family_id set (held is always false) whose metadata includes `providerCodes` (PROVIDER_SELF_HARM_INTENT, PROVIDER_SEXUAL_MINORS, PROVIDER_VIOLENCE, ...) and `source`. Policy audit_member_read (0001:520-522) lets any family member select those rows with their own JWT through PostgREST. For a flag caught only by the word list the category is absent, but whenever provider moderation contributes, its category reaches the family.
findings.repro: Probe: <scratch>/probe-audit.test.ts, test 'a guardian token reads providerCodes...'. The child's answer is 'I want to die [mock-moderation:self-harm/intent]' (labeled mock moderation). After the scan job runs, `api.apiDb.asParent({userId: owner}, select action, metadata from public.audit_events where target_id = reportId)`. For comparison, the probe selects safety_reports.screen_categories as the same role.
findings.evidence: `PROBE audit rows visible to the parent role: [{"action":"safety_report.created","metadata":{"source":"safety_screen+provider_moderation","category":"severe_risk","providerCodes":["PROVIDER_SELF_HARM_INTENT"],"screenVersion":"safety-screen.v4"}}]` while `safety_reports.screen_categories as parent: refused: permission denied for table safety_reports`.
findings.suggestedFix: Write the safety_report.created row with family_id null, as the held path already does, or move providerCodes and source into a reviewer-only record (for example a private table or an admin-only column). Add a DB/API test that a parent role cannot read any category or provider code for a flag.
findings.userImpact: The protection that hides which kind of concern was flagged (self-harm, sexual content involving minors, violence/abuse) is bypassed. This matters when the adult reading it is the subject of the child's disclosure.

findings.title: The 'All family data' export leaves out the child's homework answers, feedback, reward requests, profile notes and safety reports
findings.description: familyData() (lines 389-432) exports families, child_profiles (id, nickname, grade, age band, status, created_at), subjects, schedules, test dates, study materials, practice sets and items, attempts and the points ledger. It does not read assignments, extracted_questions (the child's transcribed answers), question_results, child_feedback (hints and safety notices shown to the child), target_answer_attempts, rewards, reward_redemptions, point_balances, child_profiles.curriculum_notes and accessibility, or safety_reports. The portal labels this kind 'All family data' (PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:64). The public policy says PencilLift collects 'Homework photos and the answers your child submits' and 'reward requests' (PrivacyPage.tsx:101-102) and offers 'a copy (export) of your family's information' (line 208). The spec asks that parents keep access to 'history, export and earned reward records' (P11, AC_CAPACITY_08).
findings.repro: Read export-build.ts:389-432: the only tables queried are families, child_profiles (six columns), child_subjects, learning_schedules, test_dates, study_materials, practice_sets, practice_items, attempts and points_ledger. `grep -n 'extracted_questions\|reward_redemptions\|child_feedback\|curriculum_notes' apps/api/src/jobs/export-build.ts` returns nothing.
findings.evidence: export-build.ts:389-432 (familyData); PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:64 `family_data: 'All family data'`; PrivacyPage.tsx:101-102 and 208.
findings.suggestedFix: Add the child's homework records to family_data: assignments, questions with the original and corrected transcriptions, results and overrides, child feedback, target answer attempts, rewards and redemptions, point balances, curriculum_notes and accessibility, and the family's visible safety reports without the reviewer-only columns. Keep answer keys and private solutions out, per the spec. Alternatively, rename the export and state in the policy what it does not contain. Add an export test that asserts the key set.
findings.userImpact: A parent who uses the export to review what PencilLift collected about their child (a COPPA parental right) does not get the child's submitted answers or reward requests, although the export is labelled 'All family data'.

findings.area: child safety / parent flag email honesty
findings.title: The flag shows 'PencilLift emailed the guardians on this account' when only one address accepted it: a bounced owner address or an unverified co-guardian is still told they were emailed
findings.description: safetyFlagEmailHandler records 'sent' once at least one verified address accepted the email (dispatcher.ts:360-382). Unverified guardians are skipped without any record (lines 341-344), and a refused address is not retried once another address accepted. Both the portal and the app then show every guardian PARENT_SAFETY_FLAG_COPY.emailSent: 'PencilLift emailed the guardians on this account about this flag when it was filed…'. The owner whose address bounced therefore reads that they were emailed, and nothing tells them that their address does not work for future flags. 'when it was filed' is also untrue when the email went out on a later retry.
findings.repro: Existing test safety-flag-email.test.ts:482-515 ('records "sent" when at least one guardian address accepted'): the owner's address rejects ('bounced'), the guardian's accepts, and the status is 'sent'. The same copy is rendered by PrivacyControlsPage.tsx:1248/1259 and parent-privacy.ts:426/432. Test 516-527: an unverified guardian gets nothing and the status is 'sent'. The suite ran green: 10/10.
findings.evidence: dispatcher.ts:341-382; contracts/src/privacy.ts:226-227; audit metadata {recipients:1, refused:1} recorded in the test while the family sees the 'emailed the guardians' line.
findings.suggestedFix: Record delivery per guardian (or at least 'partial'), show 'emailed N of M guardians' or 'your address could not be reached', and drop 'when it was filed' (or use parent_emailed_at). Consider retrying the refused addresses.
findings.userImpact: A guardian may assume the email channel works for them when it does not, and miss later flags.

findings.title: Unique (assignment_id, page_id, question_number) plus 'keep the first' silently drops a second question with the same printed number on one page
findings.description: extracted_questions is unique on (assignment_id, page_id, question_number) (0100). storeQuestions (scan-process.ts:1304-1310) skips any later extracted question whose `${pageNumber}:${questionNumber}` it has already seen ('duplicate label: keep the first'). K-8 worksheets often restart numbering per section on one page (Part A 1-5, Part B 1-5), and the extraction prompt (packages/ai/src/prompts.ts:46-55) gives no instruction to disambiguate section numbers. For such a page, Part B's questions and the child's answers to them are never stored, graded or shown, and nothing records a warning or raises uncertainty. Grading already uses synthetic refs because 'printed numbers repeat across pages' (scan-process.ts:1361), but the database key and the dedupe still assume uniqueness within a page. Candidate: whether the model emits duplicate labels depends on model behaviour, which could not be exercised here (labeled mock only).
findings.repro: Code path: extractionOutputSchema allows any questionNumber of 1-20 chars (packages/ai/src/schemas.ts:43). A model output with two questions {pageNumber:1, questionNumber:'1'} (Part A and Part B) reaches storeQuestions; the second hits `seen.has(key)` and `continue` (line 1309). Even without that guard, the insert's `on conflict (assignment_id, page_id, question_number) do update` (line 1322) would overwrite the first. No test covers duplicate labels (grep 'duplicate label' in apps/api/tests finds nothing).
findings.evidence: scan-process.ts:1304-1325; the unique constraint extracted_questions_assignment_id_page_id_question_number_key; the prompt text has no numbering guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Store a per-scan ordinal (for example position within the page) as the key and keep question_number as display text only. Or instruct the model to prefix section labels ('A1', 'B1') and, when a duplicate label still arrives, keep both with a disambiguated number and uncertainty 'high' rather than dropping one. Add a scan-process test with a duplicated label.
findings.userImpact: A child's answers to part of a worksheet quietly disappear from checking, and neither the parent nor the child is told that questions were skipped.
