findings.title: Owner churn figure can exceed 100%, and a plan upgrade counts as one lapse plus one new subscription
findings.description: loadSubscriptions divides lapsed_this_month by active_at_start, but the two counts cover different rows. lapsed_this_month is every expired, revoked or refunded row whose period_end falls in the month, including rows created in that same month. active_at_start only counts rows created before the month began. So subscriptions that start and lapse inside one month (for example a store trial or a first month that is not renewed) add to the numerator and never to the base. Separately, RevenueCat keys each ledger row by product (providerSubscriptionId `rc:<ref>:<channel>:<productId>`, providers/billing.ts:115). A tier change therefore creates a new row, and the old row expires. The same family shows up as 1 new, 1 lapsed and 100% churn even though it never left. A transfer between a family's own identities has the same effect, because the vanished row becomes 'revoked'.
findings.repro: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/billing/ops.probe.ts, run with: cd apps/api && npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.config.ts --root /home/user/claudecampsophie/apps/api --reporter=default <scratch>/ops.probe.ts -t 'P1|P2'. P1: one row has been active since August, and three rows were created on 2 Sep and expired on 9 Sep. P2: a family on pl_family_1 since 12 Aug upgrades to pl_family_2 on 14 Sep through syncFamilyFromProvider, using the labeled subscriber mock.
findings.evidence: P1 prints { activeAtStart: 1, lapsed: 3, churnBp: 30000 }, i.e. 300% churn. P2 prints { paidSlots: 2, active: 1, newThisMonth: 1, lapsed: 1, activeAtStart: 1, churnBp: 10000 }: 100% churn for a family that upgraded. SQL is at ops-metrics.ts:254-262.
findings.suggestedFix: Measure churn per family, not per ledger row: count distinct family_id in the base (a family granting access at month start) and in the lapsed set (a base family granting nothing at month end), and ignore product and tier changes within a family. At minimum, restrict lapsed to rows in the base (created_at < start) so the rate cannot exceed 100%.
findings.userImpact: The owner's company overview reports alarming or impossible churn (over 100%), and upgrades read as lost customers.

findings.title: A deleted family's subscription stays 'active' in the owner metrics and is never counted as churn
findings.description: After a family is tombstoned, RevenueCat webhooks for it are ignored with FAMILY_DELETED (webhooks.ts:448). The stale-entitlement sweep also skips it (dispatcher.ts:952 `f.deleted_at is null`). Its ledger row is therefore frozen in its last state, usually 'active'. The loadSubscriptions queries (active, subscribedFamilies, byChannel, lapsed_this_month, active_at_start) do not exclude deleted families and rely on the row's status. The result: (1) the family counts as an active, subscribed family for up to 30 days after its store period ended (the MAX_ACCESS_AFTER_PERIOD_END_MS bound). (2) It is never counted in lapsedThisMonth, because its status never becomes expired. It just drops out of the base. Account deletion is one of the main ways a family churns, and it is invisible in the churn rate.
findings.repro: ops.probe.ts -t P7. A family syncs an active pl_family_1 subscription from 5 Sep to 5 Oct. deleted_at is set on 20 Sep, the provider mock reports it expired, the clock moves to 24 Oct, and reconcileStaleEntitlements runs before loadSubscriptions.
findings.evidence: P7 prints { swept: 0, ledgerStatus: 'active', active: 1, subscribedFamilies: 1, activeAtStart: 1, lapsed: 0, churnBp: 0 }. The store expired the subscription on 5 Oct and the family was deleted on 20 Sep, yet on 24 Oct it counts as active and October churn reads 0%.
findings.suggestedFix: In loadSubscriptions, join public.families and treat deleted_at as an end of service: exclude tombstoned families from the active and subscribed counts, and count a base family deleted during the month as lapsed. Alternatively, when the tombstone is written, record a terminal ledger observation such as status 'revoked' with fetched_at at the deletion instant.
findings.userImpact: The owner sees paying families that no longer exist and a churn rate that leaves out every account deletion.

findings.title: Overview's 'recognized this month' includes network revenue the P16 revenue summary excludes as double-counted
findings.description: The P16 rule (packages/domain/src/monetization/revenue.ts revenueSummary) says fixed sponsor fees replace network revenue on the same inventory. An ad_network entry for a (category, placement, month) that already has a sponsor_direct entry is excluded and reported as a conflict. The owner overview's monetization.recognizedThisMonthCents is instead a plain SQL sum of every recognized revenue_entries row plus its adjustments (ops-metrics.ts:365-371, 477). It applies no exclusion, so the overview overstates recognized revenue and contradicts GET /v1/admin/monetization/revenue/summary for the same month.
findings.repro: ops.probe.ts -t P3. Insert two recognized 2026-09 entries on the adult_dashboard placement: sponsor_direct 50000 and ad_network 12000. Then call GET /v1/admin/monetization/revenue/summary?month=2026-09 and GET /v1/admin/overview as an MFA owner admin.
findings.evidence: P3 prints { p16Recognized: 50000, p16Excluded: 12000, overviewRecognized: 62000 }.
findings.suggestedFix: Compute the overview figure with revenueSummary(...).recognizedCents over the month's entries and adjustments, reusing the summaryFor loader, instead of a raw SUM. Alternatively, replicate the sponsor-cell exclusion in SQL.
findings.userImpact: The owner's company overview reports $120 more recognized P16 revenue than the monetization page for the same month.

findings.area: Stripe billing periods / donation rule / revenue
findings.title: A full-price Stripe renewal with sales tax (or pending proration lines) earns no $1 school donation, and the tax is booked as revenue
findings.description: mapStripeInvoiceToPeriod sets chargedCents to invoice.amount_paid, the invoice total including sales tax and any proration items. The tier and regular price come from the subscription line's price. The donation rule then requires chargedAmountCents === regularAmountCents (packages/domain/src/donations/eligibility.ts regular_tier_price). An undiscounted $39.99 renewal with tax is therefore recorded as charged 4329 against a regular 3999 and skipped as NOT_REGULAR_TIER_PRICE, so the school never gets its $1 for a full-price month. The owner revenue view also books the tax as gross revenue and estimates store fees on it. A subscription_cycle invoice carrying proration items from a mid-cycle upgrade fails the same way.
findings.repro: ops.probe.ts -t P4. With Stripe web billing enabled, a family designated to an active school since August receives a signed invoice.paid (billing_reason subscription_cycle, subtotal 3999, tax 330, amount_paid 4329, no discounts, price_family_1). Then runDonationAccrual('2026-09') and loadRevenueMonths run.
findings.evidence: P4 prints period { charged_amount_cents: 4329, regular_amount_cents: 3999, discount_cents: 0 }, accrual { familiesEvaluated: 1, accrued: 0, skipped: 1 }, accruals: 0, stripeGross: 4329.
findings.suggestedFix: Take the subscription line's own amount, or subtotal minus discounts (total_excluding_tax), as chargedCents for the donation and price comparison. Record tax separately or exclude it from gross revenue. Keep proration lines out of the subscription_period charge, for example by recording them as a separate 'proration' period.
findings.userImpact: Schools of Stripe (web) families in states that tax the subscription never receive the promised $1, and owner revenue includes sales tax.

findings.title: Payout preparation nets reversals of accruals it does not include: an August batch is reduced by a September refund
findings.description: POST /v1/admin/payouts/prepare selects accruals with donation_month <= throughMonth (line 625). It then selects EVERY unbatched adjustment for the school with no month filter and no check that the adjustment's accrual is part of this batch (lines 628-633), and marks all of them as paid in this batch. The domain intends the opposite: an adjustment on an unpaid accrual 'nets against the still-unpaid accrual in its batch' (donations/adjustments.ts carriedForward=false). In practice, a refund of a later month's unpaid accrual reduces an earlier month's payout, which can drop to carried_forward. The later batch then includes that accrual without its reversal and overpays for its months. Per-batch school statements and the paid/owed figures are wrong.
findings.repro: payout.probe.ts, with PAYOUT_TRANSFERS_ENABLED=true and a verified school. Set up accrual A for 2026-08 (+100) and accrual B for 2026-09 (+100) with its reversal (-100), then call POST /v1/admin/payouts/prepare { throughMonth: '2026-08' }.
findings.evidence: P5 prints 200 {"status":"carried_forward","netCents":0}. The school is owed exactly $1 for August, but no batch is created.
findings.suggestedFix: Select only adjustments whose accrual is in this batch (accrual_id = any(batched accrual ids)), plus carried-forward adjustments of accruals that were already paid (accrual.payout_batch_id is not null). Leave adjustments of unpaid accruals from later months for the batch that pays those accruals.
findings.userImpact: A school's payout for a month can be withheld or understated and later overstated, and the payout statements do not match the months they name.

findings.title: A refused webhook body never reaches the owner's attention list, and its event id is burned: the retry after a fix is dropped as 'duplicate'
findings.description: traceRejectedEvent (added for BUG-134 so that 'a provider event the code does not understand is visible in the admin attention list') inserts the row with status 'ignored' and error_code 'UNEXPECTED_SHAPE'. The overview's billing_events_failed attention rule counts only status = 'failed' (ops-metrics.ts:386), so the refused event never shows. There is also no other console for it (AdminHomePage says to inspect the table by hand). Worse, recordEvent reopens an existing row only when its status is 'failed' or a stale 'received' (webhooks.ts:126-128). Once the schema is fixed and RevenueCat retries the same event id, the retry answers {status:'duplicate'} and the charge, refund or state change in that event is never recorded. The same applies to rows ignored as ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH or UNKNOWN_SUBSCRIBER, which are also invisible.
findings.repro: webhook.probe.ts. POST /webhooks/revenuecat with a RENEWAL whose period_type exceeds the schema's 40-character limit, standing in for any field shape the schema refuses. Read GET /v1/admin/overview. Then re-POST the same event id with a valid body, as RevenueCat's retry would arrive after a fixed deploy.
findings.evidence: P6 prints { refusedStatus: 400, row: { status: 'ignored', error_code: 'UNEXPECTED_SHAPE' }, attentionCount: 0, retryStatus: 200, retryBody: { status: 'duplicate' }, periodsRecorded: 0 }.
findings.suggestedFix: Store refused shapes as status 'failed' (error_code UNEXPECTED_SHAPE), or include status 'ignored' with UNEXPECTED_SHAPE in the attention query. Let recordEvent reopen UNEXPECTED_SHAPE rows so that a provider retry after a fix is processed. Consider an attention line for ignored UNKNOWN_SUBSCRIBER/ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH events as well.
findings.userImpact: A store charge, refund or cancellation that the code does not yet accept is lost for good and nobody is told, even after the schema is fixed within RevenueCat's retry window.

findings.title: RevenueCat (and Stripe) requests have no timeout: one stalled connection in the entitlement sweep holds the whole tick, so deletion purges, scans and safety-flag emails never run
findings.description: createRevenueCatProvider.fetchSubscriptions calls fetch with no signal or timeout, and so do all three Stripe calls (billing.ts:179, 196, 207). The other external clients pass AbortSignal.timeout ('spec P12: every external request has a timeout', auth-admin.ts:30, supabase-storage.ts:37). runScheduledTick runs its steps one after another, and the 'entitlements' step (dispatcher.ts:1194) runs before the job ledger step (dispatcher.ts:1237). Its step() wrapper isolates failures, but not hangs. A stalled RevenueCat connection therefore stops the invocation before runJobs. The sweep orders families by oldest fetched_at, so every following 5-minute tick stalls on the same family first. For the length of a RevenueCat network stall, no deletion purge, account closure, scan or safety_flag_email job runs.
findings.repro: Probe: scratchpad/hardening/jobs-ai-r2/probes/rc-hang.probe.test.ts. It builds createRevenueCatProvider with a fetch whose promise never settles, seeds one stale entitlement and a due deletion_purge job, calls runScheduledTick and races it against 5 s.
findings.evidence: Output: `tick: still running after 5 s | revenuecat fetch calls: 1 | signal passed: [ false ] | due purge job status: queued | handler ran: false`.
findings.suggestedFix: Pass `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000)` (configurable) on every RevenueCat and Stripe request, as the storage, email and auth-admin adapters do. Also consider running the job ledger before the provider sweeps, or bounding each step's duration, so no single step can starve the ledger.
findings.userImpact: During a RevenueCat or network stall, children's scans stay in 'checking', safety-flag emails to parents are delayed, and deletions and account closures pause.

areas.notes: IMPORTANT: these findings were NOT independently verified (the three-lens verification was skipped to save hours). For each one: reproduce it first with a failing test against the current tree; if you cannot reproduce it, change nothing for it and report it in notDone as 'not reproduced' with your evidence. Only a reproduced finding gets a fix. Every new free-text request field goes through freeTextSchema (L-028); every UI list of a contract enum reads the schema's .options (L-036); a key derived from rows a retention step can delete uses the highest kept value, never a count (L-033); a pinned clock means every fixture timestamp comes from it (L-027). Lead decisions. BILL-R2-1: churn per family: the base is families granting access at month start, lapsed are base families granting nothing at month end, product or tier changes inside a family are not churn; the rate can never exceed 100%. BILL-R2-2: a tombstoned family is out of the active and subscribed counts and a base family deleted during the month counts as lapsed. BILL-R2-3: the overview's recognized-this-month figure uses the domain revenueSummary rule (sponsor fees replace network revenue on the same inventory). BILL-R2-4: the Stripe period's charged amount is the subscription line's amount (or total excluding tax), tax is not revenue, and proration lines are not part of the subscription_period charge; a full-price renewal with tax earns the $1 donation. BILL-R2-5: a payout batch nets only adjustments of accruals in the batch plus carried-forward adjustments of accruals already paid. JOBS-R2-04: every RevenueCat and Stripe request gets a timeout (AbortSignal.timeout, configurable, default 10 s) like the other adapters; tick step ordering is the lead's (dispatcher.ts belongs to another area): describe any ordering change in leadActions. Keep the approved prices and the $1 full-price donation rule. Run the affected API suites and the domain tests once at the end.

findings.title: attempt_overrides has no attempt_id index: every daily-set and review job does one full scan of all families' overrides per attempt
findings.description: loadEvidence (learning-jobs.ts:286-300) LEFT JOIN LATERALs `select ... from public.attempt_overrides where attempt_id = a.id order by created_at desc limit 1` for every attempt in the child's window, and it has to do this before the sort and LIMIT 5000 (EVIDENCE_EVENT_LIMIT). public.attempt_overrides (0100) has only its primary key. No index leads with attempt_id, so each lateral probe scans the whole table: every family's parent overrides, and the table is append-only and never pruned. The cost is (child's attempts) x (all overrides) on every daily_set_generate and thursday_review_generate job. The same missing index also makes the purge's `delete from public.attempts` check the attempt_overrides_attempt_id_fkey foreign key with a sequential scan for each deleted attempt.
findings.repro: On a migrated PG16 test DB, inside one rolled-back transaction with session_replication_role=replica: insert 200k attempts for other families and 1,000 attempts in the last 21 days for one child, add 20k attempt_overrides, ANALYZE, then run EXPLAIN ANALYZE on the loadEvidence query text (learning-jobs.ts:286-300).
findings.evidence: Plan: Nested Loop Left Join (loops=1000) -> Seq Scan on attempt_overrides, Filter: (attempt_id = a.id), Rows Removed by Filter: 20000 per loop. Execution Time: 979.806 ms for one child's evidence load. Also `set enable_seqscan=off; explain select correctness from public.attempt_overrides where attempt_id = '<uuid>' order by created_at desc limit 1` still plans a Seq Scan, so no index path exists.
findings.suggestedFix: New migration: `create index attempt_overrides_attempt on public.attempt_overrides (attempt_id, created_at desc);`. Add a schema test that asserts an index leads with attempt_id, and an EXPLAIN-based test of the loadEvidence shape.
findings.userImpact: Daily practice and Thursday review generation slow down for every child as overrides pile up across all families. At modest scale that is about 1 s per child per job and growing, which risks job timeouts or retries. Child purges slow down too.

findings.title: The inactivity sweep's lastActive runs correlated MAX() subqueries on assignments, attempts and memberships by family_id with no family index: 25.5 s for 2,000 families
findings.description: lastActive (dispatcher.ts:984-988) is evaluated for every non-deleted family in the candidate query (dispatcher.ts:1026-1037) and in the notice-void UPDATE. It computes max(created_at) from public.assignments and public.attempts and max(last_seen_at) from public.family_memberships, each `where family_id = f.id`. None of these tables has an index leading with family_id. assignments has (child_id, created_at) and (id, family_id). attempts has (child_id, skill, occurred_at). memberships has only partial active-status indexes. PG16 runs each subquery as a SubPlan per family, so the cost is O(families x (assignments + attempts)). app.inactivity_delete_family (0840) repeats the same subqueries per family. The sweep ships disabled (INACTIVITY_DELETION_ENABLED). Once the owner enables it, the spec P4 retention step cannot finish inside a Worker tick as the service grows, so inactive families are never noticed or deleted.
findings.repro: Rolled-back transaction on a migrated DB with session_replication_role=replica: 2,000 families, 50 assignments and 100 attempts each (100k and 200k rows), ANALYZE, then EXPLAIN ANALYZE of the candidate query text from dispatcher.ts:1026-1037 with the lastActive expression inlined.
findings.evidence: Seq Scan on families (rows=2000). SubPlan 2: Seq Scan on assignments, loops=2000, Rows Removed by Filter: 99950 per loop. SubPlan 3: Seq Scan on attempts, loops=2000, Rows Removed by Filter: 199900 per loop. Execution Time: 25533.835 ms. Time grows with families x rows.
findings.suggestedFix: Add `create index assignments_family_created on public.assignments (family_id, created_at desc)`, `create index attempts_family_created on public.attempts (family_id, created_at desc)` and `create index family_memberships_family on public.family_memberships (family_id)`, which turn each SubPlan into one index probe. Alternatively keep a families.last_activity_at column that the write paths stamp. Add an EXPLAIN assertion to the retention tests.
findings.userImpact: Once the owner enables inactivity deletion, the daily sweep times out, so the published inactivity-retention promise (spec P4) is not carried out. While it runs it also loads the database.

findings.title: Every AI stage admission sums all ai_usage_events by created_at with no usable index, while holding the global budget row lock
findings.description: The spend admission (spend-ceiling.ts:107-123) locks the single global spend_budgets row FOR UPDATE and then runs `select sum(cost_micros) from public.ai_usage_events where created_at >= monthStart`. The alert pass in dispatcher.ts:895-900 and ops-metrics.ts:374 run the same sum. The only index is ai_usage_events_family (family_id, created_at desc), which leads with family_id, so a created_at range cannot seek on it. The table is append-only (prevent_mutation), is never pruned, and gains several rows per scan and per practice job. Every extraction, grading, verification, coaching or practice call in the whole service therefore queues on one row lock while scanning all usage history.
findings.repro: Migrated PG16 DB, rolled-back transaction: insert 300k ai_usage_events spread over about 7 months, ANALYZE, then EXPLAIN ANALYZE `select coalesce((select sum(cost_micros) from public.ai_usage_events where created_at >= '2026-09-01T00:00:00Z'), 0)`.
findings.evidence: Parallel Seq Scan on ai_usage_events, Filter: (created_at >= ...), Rows Removed by Filter: 88480 per worker. Execution Time: 20.841 ms at 300k rows, serialized behind `for update` on the budget row. With enable_seqscan=off the planner can only do a full scan of ai_usage_events_family.
findings.suggestedFix: `create index ai_usage_events_created on public.ai_usage_events (created_at) include (cost_micros);`. Better still, keep a per-month running total (for example spent_micros on spend_budgets, incremented in the same transaction as the insert) so admission reads one row.
findings.userImpact: At scale, AI admissions serialize behind a scan that keeps growing. Scan processing and practice generation slow down for every family, and lock waits can time out, which turns into retries and dead letters.

findings.title: authenticated keeps TRUNCATE (plus TRIGGER and REFERENCES) on every public table, and TRUNCATE bypasses RLS and the append-only guards
findings.description: The Supabase default privileges (mirrored in tests/shim line 107) grant ALL on new public tables to anon, authenticated and service_role. For authenticated, every migration revokes only `insert, update, delete` (0001:474, 0100:489, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0600, 0810 and others). The anon revokes are `revoke all`. So authenticated still holds TRUNCATE, TRIGGER and REFERENCES on all ~80 public tables (families ACL `authenticated=rDxt`). TRUNCATE ignores RLS and fires no row triggers, so app.prevent_mutation on audit_events, points_ledger, ai_usage_events and consent evidence does not stop it. PostgREST does not expose TRUNCATE, so this is not directly reachable from a browser. It is reachable from any SQL that runs as authenticated: the API opens asParent transactions with `set local role authenticated` on a direct connection, so a single injection there could empty the audit log or the consent records. schema_invariants.test.ts:71-79 checks TRUNCATE for pl_child only, not for authenticated.
findings.repro: Migrated DB (harness): begin; insert one ai_usage_events row; `set local role authenticated`; set request.jwt.claims for a random user; run `delete from public.ai_usage_events`, which gives 'permission denied'; then, in a fresh transaction, `truncate public.ai_usage_events, public.audit_events, public.consent_records, public.points_ledger`, which gives 'TRUNCATE TABLE'; reset role; count is 0; rollback.
findings.evidence: information_schema.table_privileges lists TRUNCATE for grantee authenticated on every public table (admin_users, audit_events, consent_records, families, jobs, points_ledger, ...). Probe output: before=1, DELETE -> ERROR permission denied for table ai_usage_events, TRUNCATE TABLE succeeds, after=0.
findings.suggestedFix: New migration: `revoke truncate, trigger, references on all tables in schema public from authenticated, anon, pl_child;` and `alter default privileges in schema public revoke truncate, trigger, references on tables from anon, authenticated;`. Extend schema_invariants to assert that no client role holds TRUNCATE, TRIGGER or REFERENCES on any public table.
findings.userImpact: Defense in depth: one SQL-injection bug on an authenticated path could wipe audit, consent and ledger evidence for every family, with no RLS or trigger in the way.

findings.area: database / RLS policies vs API rules (Data API path)
findings.title: Direct Data API insert grants bypass the BUG-119 per-family caps and rate limits, the adult-unlock requirement and the archived-child rule
findings.description: BUG-119 added CHILD_PROFILE_LIMIT=12 and per-family rate limits in the API only (routes/family.ts:108-115, middleware/rate-limit.ts). privacy.ts adds parentReportPerUser and support.ts adds case and reply limits, also API-only. The database still grants authenticated direct INSERT on child_profiles, rewards, child_subjects, test_dates (plus DELETE), study_materials, learning_schedules, safety_reports, support_cases and support_case_messages, and their RLS policies check only family membership. The child_subjects, test_dates, study_materials, learning_schedules, safety_reports and support_* policies do not require has_recent_adult_unlock. None checks that the child is active, although the API refuses writes for an archived child (learning.ts:190). Any adult can sign up, create a family and call PostgREST with their own JWT and the publishable key. That caller can insert unlimited draft profiles, 20,000-char study materials without a PIN, or hundreds of support cases and safety reports in one bulk request. That floods the owner's support and safety queues and grows the database. The 0840/0850 comments and RV-privacy-1 treat the Data API as a real surface.
findings.repro: Probe script (scratchpad db-r2/probe_dataapi_caps.mts and probe_dataapi_queue.mts, harness asParent = role authenticated with the parent JWT): 40 inserts into child_profiles after one adult unlock; 200 inserts of 20,000-char study_materials with a session that has no unlock; a child_subjects insert for an archived child; `insert into support_cases ... select ... from generate_series(1,500)` and the same for safety_reports, with no unlock.
findings.evidence: Output: 'draft profiles inserted via Data API: 40 non-archived profiles now: 41 (API cap CHILD_PROFILE_LIMIT = 12)'; 'study materials inserted via Data API without an adult unlock: { n: 200, bytes: 4000000 }'; 'subject added to an ARCHIVED child via Data API: ok'; 'rows written by one parent in two statements via the authenticated grants: { cases: 500, reports: 500 }'.
findings.suggestedFix: Either revoke these direct insert grants and route every write through the API, whose rules then hold, or enforce the rules in the database: BEFORE INSERT triggers that take the family row lock and count per family (profile cap 12, per-hour limits via app.rate_limit_hit keyed by family), `app.has_recent_adult_unlock()` in the with-check of the learning-settings, safety and support policies, and an active-child check (child_profiles.status = 'active') in the child-scoped policies. Add Data API tests that mirror input-hardening.review.test.ts [API-AUTH-R1-04].
findings.userImpact: The BUG-119 protections are not real at the database layer. A scripted account can flood the owner's safety-report and support queues, which hides real flags, and can grow storage without bound, bypassing the PIN gate the portal relies on.

findings.area: database / indexes (parent and child per-request reads)
findings.title: Several per-request family and child queries have no index path: reward requests, test dates, study materials, devices, exports
findings.description: These queries can only be answered by a sequential scan of every family's rows. (1) The parent rewards page, rewards.ts:396-413: reward_redemptions `where r.family_id = .. and r.state in (...)`, but the only index is (child_id, requested_at). (2) The test-date list and the schedule response, learning.ts:753 and 478, plus learning-jobs.ts:386: test_dates `where child_id = .. and family_id = ..`, but the only index is (subject_id, test_date). (3) Material selection for every practice job, learning-jobs.ts:347: study_materials `where child_id = .. and created_at >= ..`, with no index at all (and rows up to 20 KB). (4) The device list, family.ts:285: child_devices `where family_id = .. order by paired_at desc`, with no index. (5) The export list, privacy.ts:667: data_exports `where family_id = .. order by created_at desc`, with no index. BUG-139, BUG-142 and BUG-155 fixed the same pattern for jobs, safety_reports and child_sessions only.
findings.repro: On a migrated DB: `set enable_seqscan = off;` then EXPLAIN (costs off) each query with literal uuids.
findings.evidence: Every plan is still 'Seq Scan on reward_redemptions' / 'Seq Scan on test_dates' / 'Seq Scan on study_materials' / 'Seq Scan on child_devices' / 'Seq Scan on data_exports' followed by a Sort, even with sequential scans disabled, so no index can serve them.
findings.suggestedFix: Indexes: reward_redemptions (family_id, state, requested_at); test_dates (child_id, test_date); study_materials (child_id, created_at desc); child_devices (family_id, paired_at desc); data_exports (family_id, created_at desc). These also serve the purge's family/child deletes.
findings.userImpact: Parent rewards, planner, devices and privacy screens, and every practice-generation job, slow down linearly with the total number of families.

findings.title: Pairing codes and expired spend holds are never pruned (twin of BUG-155)
findings.description: app.prune_session_rows (0850) prunes child sessions, refresh tokens and adult unlocks. private.child_pairing_codes rows, each 'new code' and each consumed or expired code with its code_hash, are deleted only by a family or child purge (0820:118). There is no family_id index for that delete either. private.ai_spend_holds rows left by a worker that died (expired, never settled) are never deleted. spend-ceiling.ts deletes only by id on settlement, and the admission sum `where expires_at > now` cannot use ai_spend_holds_period (period_key, expires_at) because it has no period filter.
findings.repro: grep over supabase/migrations and apps/api/src: the only `delete from private.child_pairing_codes` statements are in the purge functions (0620:212, 0710:500, 0820:118), and the only `delete from private.ai_spend_holds` statements are by id (spend-ceiling.ts:182, 244). app.prune_session_rows touches child_refresh_tokens, child_sessions and adult_unlocks only.
findings.evidence: 0850 prune_session_rows body; the index list shows private.child_pairing_codes has only pkey, code_hash and the partial live-per-child index.
findings.suggestedFix: Extend app.prune_session_rows, or add a sibling function, to delete pairing codes consumed or expired more than the horizon ago, and spend holds with expires_at < now() - 1 day. Add an index on child_pairing_codes (family_id, child_id) for the purge.
findings.userImpact: Unbounded growth of credential-derived rows (short-code hashes) and bookkeeping rows. There is no immediate user-visible failure.

findings.area: authorization / Data API grants vs API-only rules
findings.title: Rules enforced only in the API routes (12-profile cap, K-8/under-13 scope, per-family write limits, archived and deletion-pending refusals, step-up, control-character refusal) are skipped through the authenticated role's direct table grants
findings.description: Migration 0001 still grants `authenticated` (the Supabase Data API / PostgREST role) INSERT and UPDATE on public.child_profiles (nickname, grade_level, age_band, accessibility, curriculum_notes) at lines 480-483. Migration 0100_learning.sql lines 496-500 grants INSERT on child_subjects, test_dates and study_materials, UPDATE on child_subjects and DELETE on test_dates. The RLS policies on those tables check only family membership, plus a recent unlock for child_profiles and rewards. Every hardening from round 1 lives only in the Hono routes: CHILD_PROFILE_LIMIT, the K-8 contract (API-AUTH-R1-05), RATE_RULES.*PerFamily (API-AUTH-R1-04), CHILD_ARCHIVED, ownedChild()'s pending-deletion check and freeTextSchema's control-character refusal. The same adult token can write straight to the tables. docs/Owner_Actions.md #25 and the runbook treat the Data API path as reachable, and spec line 340 says 'No generic database passthrough endpoints'. The two previously reported defects (no profile cap; grade 9-12 / 14-18 accepted) are therefore fixed in the route but not in fact.
findings.repro: Probe: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claudecampsophie/b1b9c04d-3d1c-58be-b925-a948687d722a/scratchpad/hardening/api-auth/childgrant.probe.ts and learninggrant.probe.ts. Run from apps/api: `npx vitest run --config <scratch>/vitest.config.mts --reporter=default childgrant learninggrant`. Each probe runs SQL as `authenticated` through the test harness asParent, which is what PostgREST executes for a parent JWT.
findings.evidence: childgrant: `PROBE api create grade12: 400` / `PROBE direct inserts as authenticated: 20` / `PROBE non-archived profiles now: 21 (API cap is 12)` / `PROBE GET /v1/family status 200 contract parse ok? false [... path children,0,gradeLevel 'Too big: expected number to be <=8' ... ageBand invalid_value]`, so the portal's strict familyOverviewResponseSchema rejects the whole family page / `PROBE api create after direct inserts: 422 CHILD_PROFILE_LIMIT`. learninggrant, run from a session with NO PIN unlock: `PROBE API test-date for archived child: 422`, `PROBE API study-material for child under deletion: 404`, then `PROBE direct test_date for archived child (no unlock): inserted` (scope_notes containing U+0007), `PROBE direct study_material for child under deletion (no unlock): inserted`, `PROBE direct custom subjects inserted (API limit 20/h): 40`.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a forward migration that revokes INSERT/UPDATE on public.child_profiles and INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on child_subjects, test_dates and study_materials from `authenticated`, and reviews rewards and safety_reports the same way. The API already writes these rows with the service role or its own RPCs. If a Data API write must stay, move the rule into the database: CHECK grade_level <= 8 and age_band <> '14-18' (after a data check), a BEFORE INSERT trigger for the profile cap, policies that refuse archived children and children with an open deletion_request, and has_recent_adult_unlock() where the route requires it. Add a supabase/tests case per table asserting that `authenticated` can no longer write it.
findings.userImpact: A parent, or anything holding a parent's access token, can create unlimited child profiles, label children 14-18 in an under-13 product, and add learning data for archived children or children whose deletion is under way. One such row breaks the Children and Family pages, because the client rejects the family response.
